test: memory decay on the dexamethasone withdrawal timecourse
log: LOOP 247 -- MEMORY, ON A WITHDRAWAL TIMECOURSE WHERE THE FORCING TERM IS GONE
After withdrawal Phi = 0, so the equation predicts M_t = exp(-Lambda t) M_0 with
nothing else in it -- a bare decay curve, and a curve one can hold timepoints out of.
A two-timescale model has 5 parameters per gene against 3. Loop 244's Hill curve had
the same shape and LOST to a straight line once dose was held out, so W2 holds out
timepoints and W2b asks separately whether the relaxation is exponential at all.

19,814 genes, 12 timepoints [np.float64(0.0), np.float64(0.5), np.float64(1.0), np.float64(2.0), np.float64(3.0), np.float64(4.0), np.float64(5.0), np.float64(6.0), np.float64(7.0), np.float64(8.0), np.float64(10.0), np.float64(12.0)] h, 3 replicates

W1 IS THERE A RELAXATION TO FIT AT ALL?
EXP1 reduces held-out squared error by 52.5% against a constant
W1 PASS -- there is a relaxation: 52.5% of held-out error removed
W2 DOES MEMORY NEED MORE THAN ONE CLOCK?
EXP2 against EXP1 on held-out timepoints: -50999.8% of squared error
per-gene paired difference EXP1 minus EXP2: -139.014128 +/- 22.520681 (-6.2 se)
W2 FAIL -- a second timescale buys -50999.8% on held-out timepoints, against a 5% bar; five parameters per gene do not beat three
W2b IS IT EVEN EXPONENTIAL?
EXP1 against a straight line in time: -31.0% of held-out squared error
W2b FAIL -- EXP1 beats a straight line by -31.0%; over 12 hours the decay is not distinguishable from linear
W3 IS THE PROCESS NON-MARKOVIAN?
replicate 3 at t_i predicted from replicates 1 and 2 at t_{i-1} alone, against
t_{i-1} with t_{i-2} and t_{i-3}. Different replicates, so the measurement noise in
the features is independent of the noise in the target -- loop 231's L2 confound.
one step back only: 0.9936   with three lags: 0.9936
paired over 10 gene folds: +0.0000 +/- 0.0000  (+0.2 se)
W3 FAIL -- knowing t-2 and t-3 adds +0.0000 once t-1 is known, against a 0.02 bar; S(t-1) is a sufficient statistic here
W4 ARE THE FITTED TIMESCALES REAL OR GRID ARTEFACTS?
tau strictly inside the 0.15-60 h grid: 62.7%
median tau 4.40 h, interquartile range of log10(tau) 0.60 decades (2.04 - 8.14 h)
W4 PASS -- 63% of taus are off the grid edge and they span 0.60 decades
W5 CONTROL: TIME LABELS PERMUTED
timepoints reassigned: EXP1 improves -2571.1% against a real +52.5% (-4901%)
W5 PASS -- collapses to -4901% with the clock scrambled
W6 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
Twelve hours. A chromatin or structural memory with a timescale of days is outside
the window entirely and would appear as the offset C, not as a decay.
Bulk RNA. A population relaxing coherently and a population switching at different
times give the same mean curve; this design cannot separate them.
One stimulus, one cell line. Nothing here says other perturbations share these
timescales.
Withdrawal is not the reverse of addition: removing a ligand leaves receptor,
chromatin and transcript pools in states the approach to steady state never passed
through.
